clue.text: Moo from lower player in duet?

parts.note: split as MO plus O: a mo is a moment, the same as a second, and the extra O stays as written

explanation.surface: A cow lowing comes from the bottom-part pianist in a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as SECOND then O, swap SECOND for its synonym MO, and you get MO + O, the clue word Moo. The cow noise is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the second player, taking the lower part, is called by this Italian term.

clue.text: Music publisher fixed price in Dubai, say

parts.note: EMI is the British record company and music publisher
a rate is a set price or charge

explanation.surface: A record label set a price for something in Dubai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Dubai as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven federated states ruled by emirs in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: German in African port stops there

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the port's name

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria

explanation.surface: A German in an African harbour town halts there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like a verb about stopping, but organ stops are knobs selecting ranks of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe organs have stops, the controls drawn to select sets of pipes, so they are found there.

clue.text: Encyclopaedist in Germany tried miserably to grasp 10

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold, so the jumbled letters enclose the other piece
miserably means wretchedly or badly, so the word tried is mangled

parts.note: 10 is RING, and a ring is a circle shape, the letter O

explanation.surface: A reference-book writer in Germany made a poor attempt to grip a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' jumbles TRIED and 'to grasp' wraps it around O, the ring shape of 10, giving IDEROT after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot edited the great French Encyclopedie of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Playing harmoniously, wasting hours with this support

indicators.note: playing music rearranges notes, so the letters of the long word are jumbled
wasting the hours means those five letters are lost from the jumble

explanation.surface: A musician performing in harmony while time slips away is somehow funded by this payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges HARMONIOUSLY, and 'wasting' takes the letters of HOURS out of it; the seven letters left are rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony is court-ordered financial support paid to a former spouse after divorce.

clue.text: 18's sextet, minus 9

parts.note: less means minus, as in five less two
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Poulenc's group of six, take away nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is POULENC, a member of the French composers' group of six.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Six was the 1920s group of six French composers including Poulenc.

clue.text: In piece by 18, Euterpe, volume and tempo vary, new for old

indicators.note: vary means change, so all the letters are rearranged
new for old means one O, short for old, is swapped for N, short for new

explanation.surface: In a Poulenc work, the muse Euterpe, the loudness and the speed keep changing, swapping new for old.
explanation.walkthrough: Euterpe is the Greek muse of music. 'new for old' swaps one O for N in EUTERPE VOLUME TEMPO, and 'vary' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Poulenc's Mouvement perpetuel is a set of short piano pieces from 1918.

clue.text: Having scored, doze off touring gallery

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the sleepy word surrounds the gallery

parts.note: to nod off is to doze off, so the phrase gives nod
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: After scoring a goal, a player dozes while touring an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having scored' looks like sport but means written in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece that has been scored has been written out in musical notation for performers.

clue.text: Arrange tie-ins and mergers to produce 12 work

indicators.note: arrange means put in a new order, so all the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Organise product tie-ins and corporate mergers to make a Wagner piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is WAGNER; his opera Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg is about mastersingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg is a Wagner opera, a Wagner work.

clue.text: Band's 4 17s

definitions.meaning: a band is a circular hoop such as a wedding band
17 is OPERA, so four operas: Wagner's cycle of four operas is known by this short name

explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circular band, and the Ring cycle is Wagner's tetralogy of four operas.

clue.text: Two ways round tackling complex issues in evening wear

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the road letters grip the jumble between them
turned round, the pair of road abbreviations reads backwards as one unit

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
RD is short for road, another way

indicators.note: complex means involved and tangled, so the letters of issues are mixed

explanation.surface: Two people approach difficult matters from opposite directions while dressed for a formal evening.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'round', turns both road abbreviations together, and 'tackling' has them grip the scrambled letters, one pair at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress suits are formal tailcoat outfits worn by men for evening events, i.e. evening wear.

clue.text: Risk engaging nationalist composer

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the bet word holds the single letter

parts.note: to wager is to risk money on a bet

explanation.surface: Gambling on a politician of the nationalist stripe who also writes music.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle and other operas.

clue.text: What's down-at-heel Solti upset about? Not odd members of sextet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged name goes round the picked letters
upset means knocked over, so the conductor's name is rearranged
taking only the even-placed letters, second, fourth and sixth, of the word sextet

explanation.surface: Wondering what the conductor Georg Solti is upset about, since he lost the odd players in his sextet.
explanation.walkthrough: Georg Solti was a famous conductor, hence 'upset' and 'sextet' fitting the musical surface. Down-at-heel usually means shabby; here it is literal, a thing at the bottom of a heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a thin high heel, so it sits literally down at the heel of a shoe.

clue.text: See 7
First note after Bach prelude removed, cut out? What a let-down

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the cutting word goes round the rest

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

indicators.note: after places the note following the trimmed composer
the prelude is the start, so the composer's first letter is dropped

parts.note: ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, now called doh

explanation.surface: A musician drops the opening of a Bach prelude and cuts it out, which is a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ut, the medieval name for doh, is the 'First note' of the old scale; 'prelude removed' drops the composer's initial, and 'out' wraps the cutting word round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute lets its user down gently to the ground, hence a let-down device.

clue.text: Reportedly studies vibrators for 25

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than seen, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a student reads a subject, so reads means studies

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone researches vibrating devices for some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is OBOES: the reeds are the vibrating parts that make an oboe sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes use double reeds, thin strips of cane that vibrate to produce their tone.

clue.text: Some are possibly taken aback by 12's work

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the run is read in reverse
some of the words means a run of letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Some listeners may be startled by a piece of Wagner's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks AREPO from 'are possibly' and 'taken aback' reverses it. 12 is WAGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner wrote operas, so a work by him is an example of this musical drama form.

clue.text: Lemmon finally appears in The Odd Couple as barman

indicators.note: appears in places the single letter inside the jumbled letters
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the word are disordered
finally means the last letter of the actor's name

explanation.surface: Jack Lemmon's late scene in the film The Odd Couple shows him as a bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' jumbles COUPLE and 'appears in' puts N, from 'finally' on Lemmon, inside. 'barman' means a composer, who writes bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes in musical bars, so the French composer is jokingly a bar man.

clue.text: One very wealthy nearly packs 17 house of equal dimensions

indicators.note: packs means holds inside, so the opera house sits within the other pieces

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
so means very, as in so tired

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rich means wealthy
17 is OPERA, and the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera House

explanation.surface: A very rich person almost squeezes into an opera house built in neat symmetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' puts the opera house between the very-word and the shortened wealth-word; 'nearly' drops the last letter. The Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric describes things having equal measurements, as in drawings with equal scale on all axes.

clue.text: It's more moving, hence state of audience's eyes?

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters move about

parts.note: the contraction gives the three letters as written

explanation.surface: A performance is more touching, so the listeners end up teary-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ITS and MORE; it also suggests emotion, which wets the audience's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved to tears leaves eyes wetter, so the comparative describes their tearful condition.

clue.text: Supreme leader underpins popular state

indicators.note: underpins in a down clue puts the singer's name below the first piece

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
Diana Ross led the Supremes, the Motown vocal group

explanation.surface: A supreme ruler supports a popular nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme leader' looks like a dictator but is the lead singer of the Supremes.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a state in the Midwest of the United States.

clue.text: Ringed in a cloud shrouding climax to Siegfried

indicators.note: shrouding means wrapping around, so the mist encloses the letter

parts.note: mist is a low cloud

indicators.note: the climax comes at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Ringed by a cloud surrounding the climax of Wagner's Siegfried.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried is the third opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, which suits 'Ringed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means surrounded by or in the middle of, like being encircled.

clue.text: Lead in 12 17 and much else, including Tannhäuser overture

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the rearranged letters take in the single letter
else here means otherwise arranged, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the overture opens a work, so it is the opening letter of the opera name

explanation.surface: The star of a Wagner opera, and much more besides, including the opening of Tannhäuser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' is an unusual anagram signal, meaning otherwise arranged. The Flying Dutchman is a Wagner opera, and 'including' tucks in the overture's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of Wagner's opera The Flying Dutchman is its leading character.

clue.text: 12's Irish girl lives with former principal of ensemble

parts.note: lives can mean is, as in he is or he lives
old means former, as in my old school

indicators.note: the principal is the leading part, so the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wagner's Irish heroine lives on with an ex-leader of a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, the heroine is an Irish princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: They're played by 10 blowers regularly

parts.note: 10 is RING, a circle shape, the letter O

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Instruments performed by a group of ten wind players in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of blowers, BOES, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments that musicians play.

clue.text: It ends with huge outburst? Bless you (as 12 put it)

indicators.note: an outburst bursts things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A sneeze ends with a huge explosion, so a German like Wagner responds with a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outburst' rearranges IT ENDS and HUGE; the sneeze picture also fits, since this is what Germans say after one.
explanation.definitionFit: Germans say this word, literally health, to someone who sneezes, the English equivalent being bless you.

clue.text: Test allegro finale with rallentando intro

indicators.note: the finale is the end of a piece, so the last letter is taken
the intro is the opening of the piece, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A musical exam where a fast closing section follows a slowing-down introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The intro here is the first three letters, RAL, of rallentando (a gradual slowing).
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a common kind of test in music and language exams.

clue.text: Harry Potter stripped etc for group

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are disturbed and rearranged
stripped means having its outside removed, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: The boy wizard and his various other books get lumped together as a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' cuts Potter to OTTE, and 'Harry' rearranges that with ETC. Harry looks like the wizard's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a set of eight performers, so it is a musical group.

clue.text: Tenor is German — managed houses for 24's lover

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the verb holds the German word

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
ist is the German word for is

explanation.surface: A tenor who is German runs properties and plays Isolde's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is ISOLDE, whose lover in Wagner's opera is the knight of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the knight who loves Isolde in the Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera.
